rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **inductive effect** is the **permanent polarisation of σ bonds** along a carbon chain, born of an electronegativity difference and fading to nothing within three or four bonds. **−I groups** (−NO₂, −CN, −COOH, −CHO, the halogens, −OH) pull σ-electrons toward themselves, leaving the chain δ+; **+I groups** (alkyl) push electrons into the chain.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - −I: −NO₂ > −CN > −COOH > −F > −Cl > −Br > −I (typical order) - Acidity: CCl₃COOH > CHCl₂COOH > ClCH₂COOH > CH₃COOH - Carbocations: 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺ - Distance: effect ≈ negligible beyond 3–4 σ bonds

rows.label: Conditions

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The inductive effect is the permanent polarisation of sigma bonds along a chain by an electronegativity difference, classified as the electron-withdrawing (−I) and electron-releasing (+I) effects."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Three chlorines, one strong acid*** — CCl3COOH is nearly a mineral-strength acid because each chlorine tugs sigma electrons and locks the carboxylate anion into stability — inductive effect at triple strength.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Chain Reaction of Charge When a group more or less electronegative than carbon attaches to a chain, it **pulls or pushes σ-electrons through the whole chain** — the **inductive effect (I effect)**. It is a permanent polarisation, transmitted weakly along σ bonds and fading fast.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Definition and mechanism - **Inductive effect:** the **permanent displacement of σ-bond electrons** along a saturated chain, caused by an atom or group more (or less) electronegative than carbon, transmitted through successive σ bonds. - The effect is **permanent** (a ground-state polarisation) but **fades rapidly** — negligible after about the third carbon.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: −I list: NO2, CN, COOH, CHO, X, OH. +I: alkyl. Distance rule: fades by C3–C4. Acidity ladder: CCl3COOH > CHCl2COOH > ClCH2COOH > CH3COOH. Carbocations: 3° > 2° > 1°.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Stability is charge dispersal: −I groups stabilise negative centres, +I groups stabilise positive centres — acidity orders and carbocation orders are one physics read both ways.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Inductive effect (I): permanent displacement of sigma-bond electrons along a chain due to electronegativity difference; transmitted through sigma bonds; fades rapidly (negligible after ~3 carbons). -I (withdrawing): -NO2, -CN, -COOH, -CHO, -F, -Cl, -Br, -I, -OH — pull electrons, leave chain delta+.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The inductive effect's reach is short: an alpha-chloro acid is dramatically stronger than its beta-chloro isomer, and by the gamma carbon the difference has almost vanished.

rows.text: Account for the 3° > 2° > 1° carbocation stability order using +I effect.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Inductive is through σ bonds; resonance is through π:** the I effect needs no π system and dies with distance; the R effect needs conjugation and does not fade the same way.  ·  **+I does not mean "positive charge":** the plus sign records the *direction of electron push* (toward the chain), not the sign of any charge.
